name: Neo-Tengu
body:
Neo-tengus are half tengu, half members of other ancestries.

They bear striking resemblance to their humanoid counterparts, but with large black wings they can use to protect themselves and escape danger. As with other tengu, they can be regal or blustery; with a penchant for entertainment, mockery, and thievery.

Neo-Tengu Human Traits

The most common neo-tengus are half human. On the world wherein they were discovered, neo-tengus pretend to rule over the Tengu region—named for their forebears—because the humans of that reality have an easier time interacting with them than the animal kin.

Languages: A neo-tengu human begins play speaking Common and Tengu. Those with high Intelligence scores can choose any languages they want (except for secret languages, such as Druidic).
Neo-Tengu Drakorin Traits

Neo-tengu drakorin are either natural-born dragonkin with a tengu bloodline or tengus afflicted with the drakorin curse. Their snouts are more like beaks, and they bear both the prominent wings and scales of their people.

Wing Sprint: A neo-tengu drakorin’s base speed is 20 feet, but they can use their wings to gain a +10-foot racial bonus to their speed when using the charge, run, or withdraw actions.
Gliding Wings: Neo-tengu drakorin take no damage from falling (as if subject to a constant non-magical feather fall spell). While in midair, the drakorin can move up to 5 feet in any horizontal direction for every 1 foot they fall, at a speed of 60 feet per round. A neo-tengu drakorin with gliding wings cannot gain height with these wings alone; they merely coast in other directions as they fall. If subjected to a strong wind or any other effect that causes a creature with gliding wings to rise, they can take advantage of the updraft to increase the distance they can glide.

This ability replaces the afflicted drakorin’s breath weapon and the dragonkin’s +2 racial bonus on saves against magical sleep and paralysis effects.

Languages: A neo-tengu drakorin can begins play speaking Common and Tengu instead of Draconic and add both to the list of additional languages they can learn with a high Intelligence.

Neo-Tengu Dwarf Traits

Languages: A neo-tengu dwarf can begins play speaking Common and Tengu instead of Dwarven and add both to the list of additional languages they can learn with a high Intelligence.

Neo-Tengu Elf Traits

Elven neo-tengus are respected for their ability to distract potential enemies from reaching the homes of their people.

Their mimicry of both wildlife sounds and language gives them an advantage in the wooded areas with which they’re most familiar.

Nimble Faller: Neo-tengu elves land on their feet even when they take lethal damage from a fall. Furthermore, they gain a +1 bonus to their CMD against trip attempts. This ability replaces either elven immunities, keen senses, or weapon familiarity.
Sound Mimicry: As a standard action, a neo-tengu elf can make a Bluff check opposed by the listener’s Sense Motive check to recognize the mimicry, although if the listener isn’t familiar with the person or type of creatures mimicked, it takes a –8 penalty on its Sense Motive check. The elf has a +8 racial bonus on its Bluff check to mimic sounds (including accents and speech patterns, if a voice mimic) it has listened to for at least 10 minutes. The elf cannot duplicate the effects of magical abilities (such as bardic performance or a harpy’s captivating song), though it may be able to mimic the sound of those abilities. This ability does not allow the elf to speak or understand languages it doesn’t know.

This ability replaces elven magic.

Languages: A neo-tengu elf can begins play speaking Common and Tengu instead of Elven and add both to the list of additional languages they can learn with a high Intelligence.

Neo-Tengu God-Blooded Traits

God-blooded born as neo-tengu are sometimes mistaken for fallen members of their society. They must either give in to that perception or fight to prove otherwise. Many choose the former, but those who do not can still earn recognition and praise from their brethren.

Demoralizing Wings: Neo-tengu god-blooded gain Skill Focus (intimidate) as a bonus feat at creation. By unfurling their wings, the god-blooded can attempt to demoralize a single opponent as a move action, or every opponent within 50 feet that can see them as a standard action. Regardless of the result, the god-blooded can only attempt to demoralize any creature in this way once per day.

This ability replaces divine gift.

Languages: A neo-tengu god-blooded can begins play speaking Common and Tengu instead of Celestial or Demonic. Those with high Intelligence scores can choose any languages they want (except for secret languages, such as Druidic).
